nary_nodes.label: Benoît Castel crowned World Confectioner of the Year
evidence: The smell of warm bread hangs in the air at one of Benoît Castel's patisseries in Paris, where the newly crowned world's best pastry chef was hard at work testing new recipes.

Three years after fellow French pastry chef Nina Métayer was crowned champion, Castel received the UIBC award presented annually to a leading figure in the profession in recognition of their career and contribution to the trade on July 14 in Singapore.
nary_nodes.type_justification: Mentions describe a culinary award, fitting schema.org's FoodEvent as a gastronomic activity.

nary_nodes.label: Castel's mission to be world champion daily
evidence: "I have a mission: to be the world champion every day in my shop for my customers," he said, eyes twinkling.

nary_nodes.label: Benoît Castel to open new venue in Paris
evidence: Alongside his daughter Margot, he is set to open a new venue in Paris in September – a cross between a café, a restaurant and a bakery-patisserie.
nary_nodes.type_justification: Mentions refer to a venue opening, which aligns with schema.org's ExhibitionEvent for displays or launches.

nary_nodes.label: Benoît Castel collaborates with artists for Yule logs
evidence: Always in search of new inspiration, Castel also collaborates with artists to create Yule logs. "Because they're not technically limited in their ideas, it pushes us to try new things," he said.
nary_nodes.type_justification: Mentions involve collaboration with artists, fitting schema.org's VisualArtsEvent for art-related events.

nary_nodes.label: Benoît Castel creates 'pain du coin'
evidence: As a novice, he created his famous 'pain du coin', made from a variety of flours, natural quince sourdough starter, honey and Salish salt from the US Pacific Northwest.
nary_nodes.type_justification: Mentions describe the creation of named food products, aligning with schema.org's PublicationEvent for releases.

nary_nodes.label: Benoît Castel creates 'the bread of yesterday and tomorrow'
evidence: This was followed by 'the bread of yesterday and tomorrow', made from the previous day's unsold stock as part of an anti-waste initiative.
nary_nodes.type_justification: Mentions describe the creation of named food products, aligning with schema.org's PublicationEvent for releases.

nary_nodes.label: Benoît Castel discovers breadmaking in 2012
evidence: When Castel set out on his own in 2012 after working with chef Hélène Darroze, at the prestigious Hotel Costes and La Grande Epicerie de Paris, he discovered the art of breadmaking.
nary_nodes.type_definition: An event marking a significant shift in a person's professional career path.
nary_nodes.type_justification: Mentions describe a career shift in breadmaking, which is not directly covered by existing schema.org Event subtypes.
